newsitem.title: USA: NYC plans to sell more taxable debt to Europe.
newsitem.headline: NYC plans to sell more taxable debt to Europe.

text.p: New York City, which last year started selling its taxable debt in Europe, said it again would sell another floating-rate issue to that market as part of a bigger offering that mainly is aimed at domestic buyers.
In addition, the city decided to include an approximately $300 million refunding in its sale of around $600 million of new money bonds. Both these offerings will be tax-exempt, fixed-rate debt.
A New York City official has said the debt sales, which include $120 million of taxable bonds for U.S. investors, would occur on April 8.
In its release, the city only said that the offering would take place during the week of April 7.

European investors, who have shown an appetite for the city's floating-rate debt that matures in less than five years, will be offered about $50 million of taxable, floating rate bonds, which will be part of the refunding. Goldman, Sachs & Co will lead manage the deal.
Co-managers will be Bear, Stearns & Co, Citibank, J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch & Co and Morgan Stanley & Co.
The $120 million of taxable, fixed-rate bonds, which likely will mature from 1999 to 2004, will be sold through competitive auction.
Smith Barney will lead the underwriters selling the tax-exempt, fixed-rate bonds.
The other senior managers for this part of the offering will be Bear, Stearns & Co, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, and Prudential Securities.
The amount of tax-exempt, fixed-rate debt that will pay for capital improvements was boosted by $100 million to $600 million, the city pointed out in its release.
